title.title: Katok's entropy rigidity in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: in negative curvature, Liouville measure has maximal entropy only for locally symmetric metrics, all $n \ge 3$

plain: On a negatively curved space, two natural ways to pick a random path agree only on the most symmetric shapes

beats.text: Two ways to pick a random geodesic: by volume, or by maximal complexity
Katok proved they coincide only on symmetric surfaces, and conjectured it in all dimensions
The proof: equality makes the foliations smooth, then a classical theorem finishes

steps: Suppose the two ways of picking a random geodesic agree
Then the flow's stable and unstable directions must be smooth
A classical theorem then says the metric is locally symmetric

achievement.label: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture (1982)
achievement.context: Before: surfaces (Katok) and perturbative results near hyperbolic metrics (Flaminio, Humbert)
achievement.note: The novelty is the formal-symmetry classification, the step to audit

verify.ourCheck: We could not evaluate the formal-symmetry step

voice.text: Two ways to pick a random geodesic: by volume, or by maximal complexity.
If they agree, the flow's directions are smooth, and the metric is symmetric.
Claimed: they agree only on symmetric spaces.

sources.quote: Katok (Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 1982) posed it and proved surfaces
Entropy equality, through thermodynamic formalism and Livšic theory, gives $J = h + XF$ for the unstable Jacobian
In higher dimensions only perturbative results were known (Flaminio; Humbert near hyperbolic metrics)
66 pages, no Lean. The strategy is the classical one ("prove the foliations are smooth"); the novelty is in the formal-symmetry classification, which I could not evaluate.
